req.title: Echo request headers
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /headers with a JSON object whose 'headers' field mirrors the request headers received.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states GET /headers must return HTTP 200 with a JSON body whose 'headers' field mirrors the request headers. I design: (1) a positive EP test sending a custom header and asserting it appears verbatim in the response JSON; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that a header NOT sent is absent from the echoed dict; (3) a BVA boundary test sending a header with an empty-string value to probe edge handling; (4) a DT decision-table test verifying multiple custom headers are all echoed simultaneously; (5) a positive test asserting the exact HTTP status code is 200 (not 201, not 2xx range). Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant-mutation, comparison-flip, and key-omission mutants.

tests.name: test_headers_echo_custom_header_present
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /headers with custom header X-Test-Header: hello-world
trace: R-HTTPBIN-012: response 'headers' field mirrors request headers
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_echo_custom_header_present():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={'X-Test-Header': 'hello-world'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert data['headers']['X-Test-Header'] == 'hello-world'

preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Parse JSON response body and inspect top-level keys
expected: Top-level JSON object contains exactly the key 'headers'
No extra top-level keys such as 'args', 'url', 'origin' are present
trace: R-HTTPBIN-012: response JSON 'headers' field — only 'headers' key at top level per view_headers implementation

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_response_top_level_key_is_headers_only():

    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert set(data.keys()) == {'headers'}
